post.summary: ResetAllocations clears every vote in one stream (governance-gated).

parameters.description:
MsgResetAllocations clears every vote in one stream, so its emission is only
directed by voters who show up and vote again.

Votes are cast once and then persist indefinitely, so over time the split
reflects whoever was active when they last voted rather than who is active
now. This retires the whole slate at once — for one stream only; the other
stream's votes and epoch are untouched.

Options survive along with any ERTH they have already accrued, so no recipient
loses a claimable balance and nobody re-pays the address-option fee. Stake and
registrations are untouched: a human keeps their verified-human status and a
staker keeps their bond, they only have to re-express a preference. Until
voters return, the stream simply accrues to nothing.
parameters.name: body

stream, bonded stake in the capital stream.
parameters.name: body

MsgRegister registers the signer as a unique human. proof is a Barretenberg
UltraHonk (bb v5.0.0) proof and public_signals are its public signals as decimal
strings; their positions (nullifier/dsc_key/current_date) are governance params.
For the lean_poa circuit the order is [dsc_key, current_date, nullifier].
signature_algorithm selects the verifying key. The chain verifies the proof,

cosmos.base.v1beta1.Coin.description:
Coin defines a token with a denomination and an amount.

NOTE: The amount field is an Int which implements the custom method
signatures required by gogoproto.

earth.allocation.v1.AllocationKind.description:
AllocationKind identifies how an allocation option delivers its accrued ERTH.

 - ALLOCATION_KIND_UNSPECIFIED: ALLOCATION_KIND_UNSPECIFIED is an invalid default.
 - ALLOCATION_KIND_INTEGRATED: ALLOCATION_KIND_INTEGRATED resolves automatically every block via a protocol
handler selected by `handler` (e.g. "lp_rewards"). Governance-permissioned to add.
 - ALLOCATION_KIND_ADDRESS: ALLOCATION_KIND_ADDRESS accrues ERTH claimable by a fixed recipient address.
Permissionless to add (guarded by an address-option fee).

earth.allocation.v1.AllocationOption.description:
AllocationOption is a destination voters can direct an emission stream to.
Ids are per stream: option #1 of the human stream and option #1 of the capital
stream are different options.

accumulated.description: accumulated is ERTH (uerth) owed to this option, awaiting distribution/claim.

amount_allocated.description: amount_allocated is the total voting weight currently directed at this option.

claimer.description:
claimer optionally restricts who may trigger a claim on an ADDRESS option.
Empty (the default) means anyone may trigger it. Either way the payout goes
to `recipient` — a claimer only spends the gas.

handler.description:
handler selects the per-block behaviour for INTEGRATED options (e.g.
"lp_rewards"); empty for ADDRESS options.

last_reward_index.description: last_reward_index is the stream's reward index at this option's last settlement.

recipient.description: recipient is the payout address for ADDRESS options (unused for INTEGRATED).

stream.description: stream is the emission stream this option draws from.

earth.allocation.v1.AllocationWeight.description: AllocationWeight is one entry of a voter's split.

percent.description: percent is 0-100; a voter's weights must sum to 100.

earth.allocation.v1.MsgAddAddressOption.description:
MsgAddAddressOption adds an ADDRESS option payable to `recipient`.
Permissionless: any account may add one by paying params.address_option_fee
(burned).

claimer.description:
claimer optionally restricts who may trigger the claim. Leave empty to let
anyone trigger it; the payout goes to `recipient` regardless.

earth.allocation.v1.MsgAddAddressOptionR.description: MsgAddAddressOptionResponse returns the new option id.

earth.allocation.v1.MsgAddIntegratedOpti.description:
MsgAddIntegratedOption adds an INTEGRATED option, resolved every block by the
protocol handler named by `handler`. Governance-gated (authority defaults to
the x/gov module account); the handler must be registered on-chain for the
stream being added to.
MsgAddIntegratedOptionResponse returns the new option id.

earth.allocation.v1.MsgClaimAllocation.description: MsgClaimAllocation triggers the payout of an ADDRESS option.

earth.allocation.v1.MsgResetAllocations.description:
MsgResetAllocations clears every vote in one stream, so its emission is only
directed by voters who show up and vote again.

Votes are cast once and then persist indefinitely, so over time the split
reflects whoever was active when they last voted rather than who is active
now. This retires the whole slate at once — for one stream only; the other
stream's votes and epoch are untouched.

Options survive along with any ERTH they have already accrued, so no recipient
loses a claimable balance and nobody re-pays the address-option fee. Stake and
registrations are untouched: a human keeps their verified-human status and a
staker keeps their bond, they only have to re-express a preference. Until
voters return, the stream simply accrues to nothing.

earth.allocation.v1.MsgResetAllocationsR.description: MsgResetAllocationsResponse reports the epoch now in force for that stream.

earth.allocation.v1.MsgSetAllocations.description:
MsgSetAllocations sets the sender's split across the options of one stream.
The percentages must sum to 100, or be empty to clear the vote. Eligibility
and weight both come from the stream: a live registration in the human
stream, bonded stake in the capital stream.

earth.allocation.v1.MsgUpdateParams.description: MsgUpdateParams is the Msg/UpdateParams request type.

authority.description: authority is the address that controls the module (defaults to x/gov unless overwritten).

params.description: NOTE: All parameters must be supplied.

earth.allocation.v1.MsgUpdateParamsRespo.description:
MsgUpdateParamsResponse defines the response structure for executing a
MsgUpdateParams message.

earth.allocation.v1.Params.description: Params defines the parameters for the module.

address_option_fee.description:
address_option_fee is the ERTH (uerth) burned to add an ADDRESS allocation
option. Adding one is permissionless in either stream; this fee deters spam.

earth.allocation.v1.QueryOptionResponse.description: QueryOptionResponse returns a single allocation option.

earth.allocation.v1.QueryOptionsResponse.description:
QueryOptionsResponse returns one page of a stream's options. The stream
aggregates below describe the whole stream, not the page.

epoch.description: epoch is the stream's allocation epoch; votes older than it carry no weight.

reward_index.description: reward_index is the stream's current reward index.

total_weight.description: total_weight is the voting weight currently allocating in this stream.

earth.allocation.v1.QueryParamsResponse.description: QueryParamsResponse is response type for the Query/Params RPC method.

params.description: params holds all the parameters of this module.

earth.allocation.v1.StreamId.description:
StreamId selects which emission stream a message or piece of state belongs to.

The two streams run the same engine over separate state; they differ only in
where a voter's weight comes from and who is allowed to vote at all.

 - STREAM_ID_UNSPECIFIED: STREAM_ID_UNSPECIFIED is an invalid default; every message must name a stream.
 - STREAM_ID_CARETAKER: STREAM_ID_CARETAKER is the Caretaker Fund: one human, one vote. Weight
comes from a live proof-of-personhood registration and is the same for
every human.

Numbered 1 as it always was. The name changed, the wire did not — enums
travel as numbers, so existing state and any in-flight message decode
unchanged. What does change is the JSON the LCD emits and accepts, since
grpc-gateway spells enums by name.
 - STREAM_ID_GROUNDWORKS: STREAM_ID_GROUNDWORKS is the Groundworks Fund: stake-weighted. Weight is
the voter's bonded stake, normalized by the stake compounding index.

earth.allocation.v1.Voter.description:
Voter records one address's split within one stream, and the weight it was
applied with. The human stream applies the same fixed weight to everyone; the
capital stream applies the voter's normalized bonded stake, kept in sync by
the staking hooks.

epoch.description:
epoch is the stream's allocation epoch this split was cast in. A governance
reset bumps that epoch and zeroes the aggregates in one cheap operation
rather than rewriting every voter row; a record from an older epoch is
treated as having no live contribution, so re-voting starts from zero
instead of subtracting weight that has already been cleared. Epochs are per
stream: resetting one stream leaves the other untouched.

earth.dex.v1.AuctionBid.description: AuctionBid is one bidder's total contribution to the open window.

amount.description:
amount is the cumulative bid in bid_denom. Bidding more than once adds to
it; there is no withdrawal, which is what makes total_raised final at
end_time.

claimed.description:
claimed records that this bidder has taken their ERTH. The entry is kept
rather than deleted so a second claim fails loudly instead of looking like
a bidder who never participated.

earth.dex.v1.AuctionStatus.description:
AuctionStatus is the lifecycle of the genesis liquidity auction.

 - AUCTION_STATUS_PENDING: PENDING: the ERTH is pre-funded on the module account and earmarked, but no
bidding window is open. This is the state genesis starts in, and the state
an auction that drew no bids returns to, so governance can try again.
 - AUCTION_STATUS_OPEN: OPEN: accepting bids in bid_denom until end_time.
 - AUCTION_STATUS_SETTLED: SETTLED: the pool exists and bidders may claim. Terminal.

earth.dex.v1.LiquidityAuction.description:
LiquidityAuction is the one-shot genesis liquidity event.

Two thirds of the pre-mine sits on the dex module account from genesis, split
in half: one half is paid out to bidders pro rata, the other half is paired
with everything they bid to open the pool. Because both halves are equal, the
pool opens at exactly the price the auction cleared at -- bidders paid
total_raised for erth_for_bidders, and the pool is seeded with the same ratio.
There is no separate price to set and no gap to arbitrage on the first block.

The resulting LP shares are minted to the module account, which cannot sign a
transaction, so this liquidity is permanent in the same way the genesis
ANML/ERTH pool is. Nobody owns it, governance included.

bid_denom.description:
bid_denom is the asset bids are denominated in, chosen by governance when
the window opens rather than fixed at genesis -- the intended denominator
is IBC USDC, which does not exist on the chain until IBC is enabled.

claimed.description:
claimed is the running sum of ERTH already claimed by bidders. It exists so
the last claimant can be paid the remainder rather than a truncated share:
pro-rata division floors, so the individual shares do not sum to the
earmark, and without this the dust would be stranded on the module account.

end_time.description:
end_time is the unix timestamp (seconds) at which bidding closes and the
pool is created. Settlement happens in the EndBlocker, not on a message, so
it cannot be withheld by anyone declining to send one.

erth_for_bidders.description: erth_for_bidders is the earmark paid out to bidders pro rata to their bid.

erth_for_pool.description: erth_for_pool is the earmark paired with total_raised to open the pool.

pool_id.description: pool_id is the pool opened at settlement. Zero until then.

total_raised.description: total_raised is the sum of every bid placed in the open window.

earth.dex.v1.LpUnbonding.description:
LpUnbonding is an in-flight liquidity withdrawal.

The shares are escrowed on the module account rather than burned, so they stay
part of the outstanding supply for the whole unbonding period and the pool
keeps trading on the liquidity behind them — otherwise the wait would cost the
provider time without buying the pool any depth.

Because that liquidity is still working, the position keeps everything it
would have earned by staying: LP rewards, swap fees, and full exposure to the
pool. The price of leaving is time value alone — the capital is locked and at
risk for the unbonding period. The payout is therefore priced at maturity
rather than when unbonding began.

address.description: address is the provider the matured liquidity is swept to.

completion_time.description:
completion_time is the unix timestamp (seconds) at which the sweep may pay
this entry out.

shares.description: shares is the escrowed LP share coin awaiting maturity.

earth.dex.v1.MsgBidLiquidityAuction.description:
MsgBidLiquidityAuction contributes to the open auction. Bids are additive and
cannot be withdrawn.

total_bid.description: total_bid is the bidder's cumulative contribution after this message.

earth.dex.v1.MsgClaimLiquidityAuction.description: MsgClaimLiquidityAuction pays out a bidder's share of the bidder earmark.

shares.description: shares is the amount of LP shares to burn.

earth.dex.v1.MsgRemoveLiquidityResponse.description:
MsgRemoveLiquidityResponse defines the MsgRemoveLiquidityResponse message.

No amounts are returned: the payout is priced when the unbonding matures, not
when it starts, because the shares keep earning and stay exposed to the pool
in the meantime.

completion_time.description:
completion_time is the unix timestamp (seconds) at which the liquidity is
swept to the provider's wallet.

earth.dex.v1.MsgStartLiquidityAuction.description:
MsgStartLiquidityAuction opens the bidding window.

The ERTH is already on the module account and already earmarked at genesis,
so this does not move funds -- it chooses the bid asset and the deadline,
which are the only two things that cannot be known before IBC exists.

authority.description: authority is the address that controls the module (defaults to x/gov).

bid_denom.description:
bid_denom is the asset bids are denominated in. It must not already have a
pool: the dex allows one pool per spoke token, and settlement creates one.

duration_seconds.description:
duration_seconds is how long bidding stays open, measured from the block
that executes this message.

end_time.description: end_time is the unix timestamp (seconds) at which bidding closes.

earth.dex.v1.MsgSwap.description:
MsgSwap swaps token_in for denom_out. The dex routes through the ERTH hub, so
a token->token swap is executed as two hops (token_in->ERTH->denom_out).

earth.dex.v1.MsgUpdateParams.description: MsgUpdateParams is the Msg/UpdateParams request type.

authority.description: authority is the address that controls the module (defaults to x/gov unless overwritten).

params.description: NOTE: All parameters must be supplied.

earth.dex.v1.MsgUpdateParamsResponse.description:
MsgUpdateParamsResponse defines the response structure for executing a
MsgUpdateParams message.

earth.dex.v1.Params.description: Params defines the parameters for the module.

lp_unbonding_seconds.description:
lp_unbonding_seconds is how long a liquidity withdrawal waits before it is
swept to the provider's wallet. Liquidity keeps working for the pool for the
whole period, so this is what makes depth sticky rather than flight-prone.

swap_fee.description:
swap_fee is the swap fee as a percentage (points of percent): "0.3" means a
0.3% fee. It is charged in ERTH on every hop; half stays in the pool for the
liquidity providers and half is burned.

volume_depth_cap_per_day.description:
volume_depth_cap_per_day caps how much volume a pool may count toward LP
rewards, as a multiple of its ERTH reserve per day.

Volume alone is a gameable proxy for the thing the reward is buying. Half of
every swap fee returns to the pool, so an LP trading against their own pool
recovers that half and pays only the burned half — cheap enough that, left
uncapped, the reward share goes to whoever is willing to manufacture the most
throughput rather than to whoever is carrying real liquidity. Capping the
counted volume against the pool's own depth means manufacturing weight
requires posting the depth first, which is the thing worth subsidising: the
cheapest way to earn the reward becomes providing the liquidity.

It is a cap and not a switch to depth-weighting, because volume is still
what separates a pool people trade from a pool holding dead liquidity. Both
now have to be true.

Applied against the decaying volume accumulator, which holds roughly
VolumeWindowDays of volume in the steady state, so the stored ceiling is this
multiple times that window. Zero falls back to the compiled-in default; an
unset cap must not mean an absent one.

earth.dex.v1.PolBurn.description:
PolBurn is the schedule that retires the protocol's own liquidity in a pool.

Protocol-owned liquidity is the LP shares held by the dex module account,
which has no key and so can never send a MsgRemoveLiquidity. Those positions
are not permanent after all: this schedule burns them down to nothing on a
straight line, so the protocol bootstraps a market and then hands it over.
Providing liquidity is active management whose incentives do not line up with
ERTH staking, and the protocol is the worst possible manager of it; retiring
its own position is what leaves room for LPs who will actually run the book.

Retiring a slice of the position withdraws that slice's share of the reserves
and burns it, so the pool thins without its price moving.

burn_token.description:
burn_token says whether the spoke side of each retired slice is burned too.

True for the genesis ANML/ERTH pool: both assets are the chain's own, so
both are destroyed and the pool unwinds evenly to nothing.

False for the auction pool, whose spoke side is a bridged asset the chain
cannot recreate. Its ERTH is burned and the spoke asset is left in the
reserve, which walks the pool's price up and invites arbitrageurs to sell
ERTH in and take the spoke asset out. The effect is that the auction's
proceeds are spent buying ERTH off the market, and the ERTH they buy is
burned by the tranches that follow. The protocol never gets a treasury it
could spend, because a protocol swap against its own pool cannot move the
spoke asset out -- only an outside buyer can.

duration_seconds.description: duration_seconds is how long the position takes to retire completely.

shares_remaining.description:
shares_remaining is how much of the position is left. The schedule is
finished, and the entry deleted, when it reaches zero.

start_time.description:
start_time is when the line begins, in unix seconds. Zero means "the first
block that sees this entry", which is how the genesis pool's schedule is
written: the genesis file cannot know the chain's first block time.

total_shares.description:
total_shares is the size of the position when the schedule started. It is
the base of the straight line and never changes, so the amount retired is
total_shares * elapsed / duration_seconds -- a target computed from the
clock rather than accumulated per block. Chain halts and variable block
times therefore cannot make the schedule drift off its ten-year end date.

earth.dex.v1.Pool.description:
Pool defines a spoke-and-wheel liquidity pool that always pairs the hub asset
(the staking coin, ERTH) with a single spoke token.

last_volume_day.description:
last_volume_day is the day index (block time / 86400) at which `volume` was
last decayed/updated.

reserve_erth.description: reserve_erth is the hub-side reserve, denominated in the staking coin.

volume.description:
volume is the pool's decaying ERTH-denominated swap volume, used to weight
LP reward distribution. It decays exponentially per day (~7-day half-life
window), so recent trading dominates.

earth.dex.v1.QueryAuctionBidResponse.description: QueryAuctionBidResponse is the response type for Query/AuctionBid.

claimable.description:
claimable is the ERTH this bidder can take right now: their pro-rata share
after settlement, or zero before it.

earth.personhood.v1.MsgRegister.description:
MsgRegister registers the signer as a unique human. proof is a Barretenberg
UltraHonk (bb v5.0.0) proof and public_signals are its public signals as decimal
strings; their positions (nullifier/dsc_key/current_date) are governance params.
For the lean_poa circuit the order is [dsc_key, current_date, nullifier].
signature_algorithm selects the verifying key. The chain verifies the proof,
verifies dsc_der against the CSCA trust store and binds it to the proof's
dsc_key, pins current_date to block time, and dedups on the nullifier.

affiliate.description: affiliate is the optional referrer address (must be a registered human).

dsc_der.description:
dsc_der is the DER-encoded Document Signer certificate that signed the
passport's SOD. The chain verifies it chains to a trusted CSCA and is not
revoked, then recomputes its commitment and requires the proof's public
input to match — so the proof is bound to this specific signer.

proof.description: proof is the Barretenberg UltraHonk proof bytes (bb v5.0.0, poseidon2 flavor).

public_signals.description:
public_signals are the circuit public signals as decimal strings; positions
are governance-configured (nullifier_index / dsc_key_index / current_date_index).

buyback_max_accrual_seconds.description:
buyback_max_accrual_seconds caps how much elapsed time one buyback may mint
for, bounding the catch-up after a halt or a long run of skipped windows.

It is the same concern that keeps last_buyback out of genesis exports: time
during which the buyback did not run is not emission that was earned, and
minting it in a single trade would dump an arbitrarily large ERTH order into
the ANML pool. Zero falls back to the default.

buyback_max_deviation_bps.description:
buyback_max_deviation_bps is how far above the time-weighted average price
the pool's spot price may sit and still be traded into, in basis points.

This is the anti-sandwich control. The buyback is a predictable, fixed-size
market buy from a known address, which is the ideal target: push the price
up, let the protocol buy high, sell back. Refusing to trade when spot has
been pushed above the average defeats that — the manipulated buy simply
does not happen, and the emission accrues to the next window instead of
being spent at the manipulated price.

Deliberately one-sided. Spot *below* the average means the buyback gets more
ANML per ERTH, which is the outcome the mechanism wants; gating on it would
only stall emission for no gain. An attacker who pushes the price down is
selling ANML cheaply to a protocol that is trying to buy it.

Zero falls back to the default: an unset deviation bound must not mean "any
deviation is acceptable", which is the same failure mode documented on
current_date_max_skew_seconds above.

buyback_twap_window_seconds.description:
buyback_twap_window_seconds is the minimum age of the price observation the
ANML buyback prices against, and therefore also its cadence: emission
accrues until the window has elapsed, then buys in one trade.

A per-block buyback cannot be protected by a TWAP, because a window one
block long is the spot price. Accruing between trades is what creates a
window to average over; nothing is lost by waiting, since the accrued
amount is minted in full when the trade fires. Zero falls back to the
default.

country_daily_registration_floor.description:
country_daily_registration_floor and country_daily_registration_share_bps
are the same bound one level up, per ISO 3166-1 issuing country.

The per-signer cap alone is bypassable by exactly the attacker it is aimed
at: a compromised CSCA can mint fresh Document Signers at will, and each new
one arrives with a full unused daily allowance. Bounding the country is what
makes the number of signers stop mattering. Necessarily looser, since a
country legitimately has several signers active at once.

current_date_index.description:
current_date_index is the public-input position of the prover-supplied
current_date (YYMMDD) in the register circuit's public inputs. The circuit
proves the passport expiry >= current_date; the chain pins current_date to
block time (see current_date_max_skew_seconds) so an expired passport
cannot be registered by backdating current_date.

current_date_max_skew_seconds.description:
current_date_max_skew_seconds bounds how far the proof's current_date may
differ from the block time.

Zero is rejected by Params.Validate and disables registration outright. It
is not "no tolerance": the skew comparison is the only thing tying the
prover-supplied current_date to real time, so skipping it lets any expired
passport prove out against a backdated date.

dsc_daily_registration_floor.description:
cap = max(floor, share_bps * yesterday's network registrations / 10000)

This is the automatic brake on a compromised or complicit signer. A signer
whose key is stolen can mint unlimited valid passport proofs, and until
there is a cap the only thing standing between that and unlimited
registrations — each drawing ANML daily and carrying democratic-pillar vote
weight — is a human noticing a counter and governance voting to revoke,
which takes days. The cap cannot prevent the compromise; it bounds what the
compromise is worth before anyone acts.

Two terms because neither works alone. A fixed floor is either too tight for
a country whose adoption takes off or too loose to matter once the network
is large. A pure share is meaningless at genesis, when a handful of
registrations make any signer look dominant. Taking the larger means the cap
never falls below the floor and widens on its own as the network grows,
instead of waiting on governance to keep raising a constant.

Scaled against yesterday's completed day, not today's running total: see
previous_count in RateCounter.

Hitting the cap is a deferral, not a ban. The registration is refused with
an error saying to retry, and the day rolls. Suspending the signer outright
would mean one compromised key can lock every genuine holder of that
country's passports out until a governance vote completes — a worse failure
than the one being prevented. Zero on either falls back to the default.
dsc_daily_registration_floor.title:
dsc_daily_registration_floor and dsc_daily_registration_share_bps bound how
many registrations one Document Signer may produce in a day:

dsc_key_index.description:
dsc_key_index is the public-input position of the DSC commitment —
Poseidon2 over the Document Signer's canonical public key. The chain
recomputes it from the certificate in MsgRegister and requires equality,
which is what binds the proof to a specific, CSCA-verified signer.

dsc_verification_gas.description:
dsc_verification_gas is the gas charged for one Document Signer certificate
chain verification, consumed immediately before it runs. Cheaper than the
SNARK by orders of magnitude, but it is still an unmetered public-key
operation on attacker-supplied bytes. Zero falls back to the default.

nullifier_index.description:
nullifier_index is the public-input position of the nullifier
(zkPassport's scoped_nullifier) in the register circuit's public inputs.

proof_verification_gas.description:
proof_verification_gas is the gas charged for one UltraHonk registration
proof verification, consumed immediately before the verifier runs.

Without it the most expensive operation on this chain is free. The block gas
limit is the only bound on how much CPU one block may demand, and it can
only bound work that is metered: an unmetered verifier lets a block full of
deliberately-invalid proofs stay far under the gas limit while taking
seconds of wall-clock time on every validator, which is a liveness failure
rather than a fee problem. A minimum gas price does not substitute — it
bounds what the attacker spends, never what a block costs to execute.

Governance-tunable because the cost tracks the circuit: a larger register
circuit verifies more slowly, and the charge has to follow it. Re-benchmark
(BenchmarkVerify in zk/ultrahonk) whenever the verifying keys change.
Zero falls back to the compiled-in default rather than disabling the charge,
since "unset" must never be the cheapest configuration.

registration_sweep_limit.description:
registration_sweep_limit caps how many registrations BeginBlocker may retire
per block, across every reason for retiring one.

A single budget, not one per sweep, because nothing meters this work. Block
gas bounds transactions; BeginBlock runs on an infinite gas meter and
consumes no block gas, so the only ceiling on automatic per-block work is
the one written here. Two sweeps with separate caps would each look
reasonable while their sum — the number that actually decides how long a
block takes — was never chosen by anyone.

Exceeding it is safe: the backlog drains over following blocks and a
registration_sweep_capped event is emitted. That event persisting is the
signal to raise this. Zero falls back to the compiled-in default.

registration_validity_seconds.description:
registration_validity_seconds is how long a registration stays valid before
it must be renewed.

verifying_keys.description:
verifying_keys maps a passport document/circuit id to the Barretenberg
UltraHonk (bb v5.0.0) verifying-key blob for that register circuit. The prover
(phone) picks the circuit matching its passport; the chain selects the key by
the same id. Governance manages the set. Empty disables registration until
keys are configured.

earth.personhood.v1.Registration.description:
Registration is a proof-of-personhood record: one unique human, deduped by the
zk nullifier, bound to a wallet address.

country.description:
country is the DSC's ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 issuing country, or "" when the
certificate carries no country attribute.

dsc_key.description:
dsc_key is the Poseidon2 commitment to the Document Signer that produced the
registration proof — the same value the circuit exposed publicly. Recording
it is what makes a compromised signer's registrations enumerable.

last_anml_claim.description: last_anml_claim is the unix time (seconds, UTC midnight) of the last ANML claim.

nullifier.description: nullifier is the unique per-person value output by the registration proof.

registered_at.description: registered_at is the unix time (seconds) of registration.

earth.pki.v1.MsgAddCsca.description: MsgAddCsca adds a CSCA certificate (DER) to the trusted master list.

earth.pki.v1.MsgRevokeDsc.description:
MsgRevokeDsc withdraws trust from a Document Signer, e.g. after its private
key is known to be compromised. Identified by the certificate itself so the
authority does not have to hand-encode a canonical public key.

Because every registration publicly names the DSC that produced it, revoking
one also makes the affected registrations enumerable.
